In this article AMD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:42 01:42 Shares of AMD fall after Hunterbrook discloses short position Squawk on the Street Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem." Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD. The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers." CNBC did not independently verify this information. Hunterbrook also said that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips." Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon AMD, 1-day The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia. "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson said in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity." Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls. AMD continued to slide after-hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m. Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.   "200  RELEASE Contacts: William W. Sheehan II Connie Kao Executive Vice President, Senior Vice President, Investor Relations Chief Financial Officer (925) 965-4668 (925) 965-4150 connie.kao@ros.com Ross Stores Reports Strong Third Quarter Sales and Earnings Results Updates Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Outlook Dublin, California, November 19, 2026 -- Ross Stores, Inc. (Nasdaq: ROST) today reported financial results for the 13‑week quarter ended October 31, 2026. Highlights: • Total sales for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 increased a robust 12% versus last year, with comparable store sales up a strong 8%, primarily driven by customer traffic. • Third quarter operating margin of 12.3% increased 70 basis points compared to last year, above the Company's plan of 11.7% to 12.0%. • Earnings per share for the third quarter of $1.91 exceeded our guidance of $1.75 to $1.83. • During the quarter, opened 51 new stores, including 41 Ross and 10 dd's DISCOUNTS, completing 2026 store opening plan of 115 new locations. Jim Conroy, Chief Executive Officer, commented, “We are extremely pleased with our third quarter sales and earnings growth, particularly given the more challenging comparisons we faced. Results exceeded our expectations as our marketing initiatives continue to attract more customers while our compelling combination of great brands at exceptional values and an enhanced store experience continued to resonate. As a result, customer traffic remained the primary driver of our comparable store sales growth. We are encouraged by the broad-based strength of our results and the continued positive response from customers to our brands, values, and shopping experience.” ROSS STORES, INC. 5130 Hacienda Drive, Dublin, CA 94568 (925) 965-4400 Third Quarter and First Nine Months Results Sales for the third quarter increased 12% to $6.3 billion, up from $5.6 billion in 2025. Comparable store sales rose a strong 8% for the quarter on top of a 7% gain last year. Net income was $606 million versus $512 million last year, while earnings per share were $1.91 compared to $1.58 per share in the prior year period. For the first nine months of fiscal 2026, sales grew 15% to $18.5 billion, up from $16.1 billion in 2025. Comparable store sales for the nine-month period were up 11%. Net income was $2.1 billion versus $1.5 billion last year, while earnings per share were $6.59 compared to $4.61 per share in the prior year period",
